directions: The sentence of death for the offence under Section 302 is set aside and substituted with that of rigorous imprisonment for a period of 25 (twenty-five) years without remission.

The sentence imposed for offences under Section 364 IPC (10 years S.I. and Rs. 10,000/- fine) and Section 6 of the POCSO Act (life imprisonment and Rs.10,000/- fine) shall run concurrently with the sentence of rigorous imprisonment for a period of 25 years without remission.
The Special Leave Petition is dismissed.
The dismissal of the Special Leave Petition will not debar the petitioner from availing such remedies as are available under law.

issue.issue_text: Whether the sentence of death for the offence under Section 302 should be upheld.

facts: The appellant was convicted for the kidnapping, brutal sexual assault, and murder of a four-year-old boy.
The Trial Court sentenced the appellant to death for the murder, and the High Court confirmed this sentence.
law: A death sentence is typically reserved for the 'rarest of rare' cases.
When sentencing, courts must consider the possibility of the offender's reformation.
A sentence should be proportionate to the crime committed.
Courts can impose a fixed-term sentence of imprisonment without the possibility of remission as an alternative to a standard life sentence or the death penalty.
application: The Supreme Court first upheld the appellant's conviction, finding the evidence conclusive.
In considering the death sentence, the Court found that this was 'not a case where possibility of reformation is completely ruled out'.
Because reformation was possible, the Court concluded that the case 'falls short of the rarest of rare category' required for a death sentence.
However, the Court also found that a standard life sentence (which often works out to 14 years) would be 'grossly disproportionate and inadequate' given the heinous nature of the crime.
Therefore, the Court decided that a sentence of imprisonment for a prescribed period without remission would be a 'just desert' and proportionate to the crime.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court rejected the death sentence, setting it aside and substituting it with a sentence of rigorous imprisonment for a period of 25 years without remission.

issue.issue_text: Whether the conviction of the appellant should be maintained.

facts: The court relied on a chain of circumstances presented in the case, one of which was that the appellant was the last person seen with the deceased.
law: For a conviction to be upheld based on circumstantial evidence, the circumstances must be fully established, consistent only with the hypothesis of the accused's guilt, not explainable by any other hypothesis, be conclusive in nature, and form a complete chain pointing to the accused's guilt.
application: The Court found that the circumstances enumerated in the case were fully established by the prosecution. It concluded that these established facts were consistent only with the guilt of the appellant and could not be explained by any other reasonable hypothesis. The Court determined that the chain of circumstances was so complete and conclusive that it pointed directly to the appellant's guilt for the charged offenses.
reasoning.conclusion: In view of the complete and conclusive chain of circumstantial evidence, the Supreme Court upheld the conviction of the appellant as imposed by the Trial Court and confirmed by the High Court.

issue.issue_text: Whether the appeals should be allowed.

facts: The case involved Criminal Appeal Nos. 5412-5413 of 2024 and a separate Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No. 9162 of 2021.
application: The Supreme Court's decision was based on a consideration of the 'overall facts and circumstances' of the case.

The text indicates that the court was satisfied with its conclusion 'for the reasons stated above' and in view of the 'circumstances elucidated above', although the specific details of these reasons and circumstances are not provided in the excerpts.
Based on this unstated analysis, the court determined that the appeals should be partly allowed.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that the appeals should be partly allowed.

issue.issue_text: Whether the Special Leave Petition should be allowed.

facts: The court was considering Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No. 9162 of 2021.
application: The Supreme Court noted that it had already passed a judgment in a related case, specifically Criminal Appeal (Arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 9015-9016 of 2019).
In light of that judgment, the court determined that no separate orders were required to be passed in this particular Special Leave Petition.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court dismissed the Special Leave Petition. However, it clarified that the dismissal would not prevent the petitioner from availing other legal remedies in accordance with the main judgment rendered in the related appeal.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: For a statutory presumption to be available, the foundational facts must be proved to exist beyond a reasonable doubt, and not merely by a preponderance of probability.
obiter: In cases based on circumstantial evidence, the circumstances should be of a conclusive nature and tendency.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The Court upheld the conviction, finding that the circumstances established by the prosecution were fully established, consistent only with the hypothesis of the guilt of the accused, conclusive in nature, and formed a complete chain pointing to the conclusion that the appellant is guilty. However, while the crime was heinous, the case fell short of the 'rarest of rare' category required for a death sentence. A standard life sentence of 14 years was deemed grossly disproportionate and inadequate, necessitating a modified sentence of imprisonment for a prescribed period without remission to be proportionate to the crime and maintain public confidence in the legal system.
legal_tests_applied: For a conviction based on circumstantial evidence, the circumstances must be fully established, consistent only with the hypothesis of the guilt of the accused, not explainable by any other hypothesis, be of a conclusive nature and tendency, and the chain of circumstance must be so complete as to point to the conclusion that the appellant is guilty.
The death penalty is reserved for cases that fall into the 'rarest of rare' category.
why_appellant_lost: The circumstances enumerated by the prosecution were found to be fully established, consistent only with the hypothesis of the guilt of the accused, conclusive in nature, and the chain of circumstance was so complete as to point to the conclusion that the appellant is guilty of the offences charged.
The Special Leave Petition was dismissed.
why_respondent_won: The prosecution successfully established that the circumstances were consistent only with the hypothesis of the guilt of the accused, were conclusive in nature, and that the chain of circumstance was so complete as to prove the appellant's guilt.
policy_considerations: A sentence of life imprisonment which normally works out for 14 years would be grossly disproportionate and inadequate considering the nature of the crime.
A sentence of imprisonment for a prescribed period without remission would alone be proportionate to the crime and also not jeopardize the public confidence in the efficacy of the legal system.
